A.explanation: 86, 87 and 88 are the proton numbers $Z$ from the lower numbers in $^{211}_{86}\text{Rn}$, $^{210}_{87}\text{Fr}$ and $^{212}_{88}\text{Ra}$, not the neutron numbers.

C.explanation: 211, 210 and 212 are the nucleon numbers $A$, which count protons plus neutrons, not neutrons alone.

D.explanation: 297, 297 and 300 correspond to $A+Z$, adding protons twice instead of subtracting them from the total nucleons.
